Origins and Settlement History of the Naraguta Highland People

By Elder Yakubu Magaji & Historical Research Cell

The Anaguta represent one of the foundational indigenous populations inhabiting the northern apex of the Jos Plateau. Their continuous settlement along the Naraguta hill cluster predates modern colonial cartography by hundreds of years.

The Granite Tors as Natural Fortresses

Early settlers established their homesteads amidst granitic rock clusters, taking advantage of natural caves as defensible shelters and cold highland breezes that kept grain dry and safe from pests.

Early Metallurgy

Prior to industrial mining, Anaguta craftsmen operated small-scale bloomery furnaces along the Delimi river, smelting native cassiterite and iron into blades, arrowheads, and household tools.
